posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
618 YishunNoticed the pork lard had some skin and wanted to revisit. This time I noticed the carrot cake stall was open and asked if I can order one. Old aunty said “Yes can and won’t take so long.”. I the ordered a $5.50 HKM + $4 ingredients + egg fried into noodles and + 1 sunny side up. Don’t know why but had two yolks. I think it’s quite common for her eggs to have two yolks.  Carrot cake was just superb. Won’t elaborate but I get why the queue is so long and I won’t mind ordering it and wait while I eat something else.  HKM was mild in flavor but since I added eggs and there were so much ingredients, it was quite a healthy meal. The pork lard and skin….plenty of good fats and collagen. I understand why so many people revisit. It’s relatively healthy compared to some others, and it’s quite a big portion. Prawns were huge and firm, and was nicely seasoned. Glad to have this as the last HKM for this lunar new year. I couldn’t finish and had to waste food. Sigh. I made it up by fasting the rest of the day and made it my only meal for the day. 618 Yishun Ring Rd, Singapore 760618

This stall needs no introduction. If you don’t know this stall, please leave the group. Anyway, jokes aside. Heard of this legendary stall so many times and decided to come try (first time) since I was in the vicinity. Could literally smell the wok hei when I approached the stall. Confirm ho seh liao. Ordered a $7 portion, pretty decent serving size. Waited about 10 mins.First bite. WOK HEIIIII. Solid. Really love the wok hei and mild umami. Noodles were fried really well and still slightly wet and the gooey zhup was just out of this world. Not sure if they offered pork lard, but their pork slices were thick and chunky. 3 medium to large size prawns were fresh. No sotong though. Chilli was not the typical sambal I like but this was quite ok, spicy and sour, goes quite well with the noodles. Overall, superb plate of noodles for me and superb value for $7. PS. I saw their sign board got opeh leave for takeaway, anyone knows if really have? Didn’t had a chance to ask as they were really busy with dinner service.

posts.text:
I must confess, for a HKM aficionado, I have not tried Nam Sing. But definitely not for the lack of trying. Many times I reached Old Airport market only to find them sold out and at other times, the wait was more than 40 min, which prompted me to opt for the other famous brand Yi Ji.This brand has survived since 1960s, and it has a fierce following who defends their style, since it could be their growing up comfort food.So let's be objective. The ingredients were definitely fresh and I found the sotong especially to be very fresh and springy. Chilli to me was disappointing, there is only cut red chilli, and not that of the spicy kind. I hear that's the way the ancients have it, before the advent of belachan and chili padi to the dish.Stock wise not as strong flavored as other well known heavyweights, not so much of prawn umami, instead I can taste they opted for slight seafood umami combined with lots of egg. Overall the dish felt very healthy and not too sinful a delight for a HKM. I can see why this could be a comfort food for many, but it unfortunately doesn't hit strong flavorful notes I would have preferred.@Nam Sing hokkien fried meeOld Airport FC
